column1: # The search synonym and abbreviation table (T-0204).
# Four tab-separated columns, no header row:
# A `kind` row maps a word a person types to an OpenStreetMap category value.
# The query resolves `term` and `expansion` as the same query word, so
# when the row is named "Подорожник" or "Пульс". The expansion must be a word
# the builder indexes from the kind string: kinds are indexed as their
# `key=value` words, so the value word ("pharmacy") is what to use. A `kind`
# row costs nothing in the index: it is read on the query side only.
# An `abbreviation` row maps a short street word to its full word. It is read
# on both sides: the builder rewrites an occurrence in a place's own name
# (a row spelled "пр-т Червоної Калини" indexes like "проспект ..."), and the
# query rewrites the typed text the same way. The builder side is what keeps
# the bytes of a name that already uses the short form searchable by the full
# Columns are folded before use: lower case, accents and apostrophes dropped
# (`fold::normalise`). Write an entry the way a reader types it; the fold is
# applied on load. `term` and `expansion` must differ, or the row is dropped.
# To add an entry, add one line and run `cargo test --locked` in
# `rust/grass-core`; `synonym::tests` checks the shipped table parses and that
# no expansion is empty. Keep a `kind` expansion to the OSM value word: the
